scenes.title: Contract ending
scenes.caption: What it says, and what you can do.
scenes.say: Your phone contract is coming to an end. Here's what that means, and what you can do about it.

scenes.title: The end date
scenes.caption: Your 24-month contract ends on 5 January 2027.
scenes.say: Your twenty-four month contract with Skyline Mobile ends on the fifth of January, twenty twenty-seven. The phone is then paid off, so it's yours.

moves.cue: ends on the fifth of January

scenes.title: Do nothing
scenes.caption: Doing nothing moves you to a £32 plan.
scenes.say: Do nothing, and you move to the standard plan at thirty two pounds a month. That's ten pounds more than now.

scenes.title: Three choices
scenes.caption: Upgrade, go SIM-only, or leave.
scenes.say: You have three choices. Upgrade to a new phone, keep your phone with a SIM-only deal, or leave for another network.

scenes.title: The prices
scenes.caption: Upgrade from £25, SIM-only from £8.
scenes.say: Upgrades start at twenty five pounds a month for two years. SIM-only starts at eight pounds a month for a year, with thirty gigabytes.

scenes.title: Leaving
scenes.caption: Text PAC to 65075 and keep your number.
scenes.say: To leave, text PAC to sixty five oh seven five. You get a free code for your new network, and keep your number.

scenes.title: Choose now
scenes.caption: Use the Skyline app, or call 150.
scenes.say: To choose, open the Skyline app, or call one five oh from your mobile. Do it before the fifth of January.

faults: scene 2: the label "Yours to keep" is too long and runs into its neighbours; the calendar and clock badge crowd each other
scene 3: Skyline Mobile moved from far-right to right; the cast should keep its spots
scene 3: the count passes through £31 and ends on £32, but the phone is not what costs the money, and a warning on the person shows no rise; coins could show the cost
scene 4: the choices are shown with a briefcase for SIM-only and a globe for leaving; a bag or world is not a SIM or another network, and the third choice only arrives at the end
scene 5: the table has a row 'Now £22/month 20GB' that Peter never says, the 30GB for SIM-only is missing, and the text is hard to read
scene 6: a letter flies for a text message and the tick lands on the network before it is told; the phone label 'Text PAC' is not the phone's name

scene 7: the label 'Skyline Mobile' is too long and crowds its neighbours; Reelie stands next to the mast and the wave from the person goes through the phone to the mast, which does not show calling or the app
